title: sou350121/VLA-Handbook
summary: VLA-Handbook is a Chinese, practice-oriented learning and interview guide for algorithm engineers trying to enter Vision-Language-Action robotics. It narrows the usual CV/NLP interview-prep lens to robotics-specific problems, making it useful as a focused roadmap for people who already know the broader ML stack but need to understand what changes when perception, language, and action are tied to embodied systems.

title: NVlabs/ProtoMotions
summary: ProtoMotions provides a GPU-accelerated simulation and learning stack for training physically simulated digital humans and humanoid robots. It is aimed at building and evaluating motion policies in high-throughput physics simulation, making it useful for researchers working on humanoid control, imitation, and embodied AI.

extra.full_text: ProtoMotions is a GPU-accelerated simulation and learning framework for training physically simulated digital humans and humanoid robots.

title: DravenALG/awesome-vla-wam
summary: DravenALG/awesome-vla-wam is a curated reading list for Vision-Language-Action models and World Action Models, collecting research that connects perception, language understanding, action generation, and world modeling for robotics and embodied AI. It is useful as a map of the fast-moving VLA/WAM literature rather than a runnable tool, helping researchers quickly find relevant papers, methods, and adjacent resources in one place.

title: leggedrobotics/pace-sim2real
summary: PACE targets sim-to-real transfer for legged robots by systematically identifying actuator and joint dynamics using only standard joint encoders. The repo appears useful for teams trying to close the reality gap without extra sensing hardware, especially when unmodeled drivetrain or joint behavior is what keeps simulated controllers from matching real robot performance.

extra.full_text: PACE: A systematic approach for sim-to-real transfer of legged robots, identifying actuator and joint dynamics with standard joint encoders.

title: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground
summary: MuJoCo Playground is an open-source library for training robot policies with GPU-accelerated simulation in MuJoCo, aimed at making robot learning experiments faster and easier to move toward real hardware. It is most useful as a practical sim-to-real toolkit: researchers can prototype and benchmark control policies in high-throughput environments, then use the same ecosystem to study transfer from simulation to robots.

extra.full_text: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for writing GPU-accelerated simulation code, aimed at robotics, physics-style simulation, and machine learning workloads. It is useful when you want Python-level ergonomics while still compiling compute-heavy kernels for fast execution on NVIDIA GPUs.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable setup for building robotics simulation environments and evaluating learned policies across different robot bodies, objects, and scenes. It is meant to make prototyping robot-learning tasks faster and more scalable, especially when a researcher wants to swap embodiments or environment components without rebuilding the whole simulation stack.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: basic-locomotion-isaaclab provides an IsaacLab DirectEnv setup for training and testing quadruped locomotion policies across multiple robot platforms. It is useful as a compact starting point for researchers who want to move policies through simulation, sim-to-sim transfer, and eventually sim-to-real deployment without rebuilding the environment plumbing from scratch.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: Toni-SM/skrl
summary: skrl is a modular reinforcement learning library that lets researchers build and run RL agents across PyTorch, JAX, and NVIDIA Warp backends. It is aimed at practical experimentation across common simulation stacks, including Gymnasium/Gym, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and MuJoCo Playground, making it useful when comparing algorithms or moving policies between robotics environments.

extra.full_text: Modular Reinforcement Learning (RL) library (implemented in PyTorch, JAX, and NVIDIA Warp) with support for Gymnasium/Gym, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, MuJoCo Playground and other environments

title: iit-DLSLab/sim2real-robot-identification
summary: Joint calibration code for quadrupeds and manipulators aimed at reducing the mismatch between Isaac Lab or MuJoCo simulations and real robot hardware. It appears useful as a practical sim-to-real utility: identify and correct joint-level offsets or calibration errors before transferring controllers or policies, so the simulated robot’s kinematics line up more closely with the physical platform.

extra.full_text: A joints calibration routine for quadrupeds and manipulators to facilitate sim-to-real transfer from isaaclab and mujoco to real robots

title: facebookresearch/project_superdex
summary: SuperDex is a unified robotics simulation platform that combines a purpose-built physics engine, authoring tools, and a scalable reinforcement learning interface. It is aimed at building and training robot behaviors in simulation, with VR teleoperation already part of the workflow and more capabilities planned in later releases.

extra.full_text: SuperDex brings together a purpose-built physics engine, robotics authoring tools, and a scalable reinforcement learning interface in a unified simulation platform, with VR-based teleoperation and additional capabilities planned for future releases.

title: dartsim/dart
summary: DART is a research-oriented C++23 physics engine aimed at robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings for easier experimentation. It is useful when a project needs simulation infrastructure for articulated bodies and robot dynamics rather than a black-box application layer.

extra.full_text: Research-focused C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings

title: OpenBMB/SimpleMemVLA
summary: SimpleMemVLA adds native video memory to vision-language-action models by keeping a timestamped visual history and supporting exact streaming inference over long horizons. It is aimed at robot manipulation settings where the model needs to use past observations directly rather than relying only on the current frame or compressed state, making it useful for temporally extended tasks that require remembering what happened earlier.

extra.full_text: Native-video memory for vision-language-action models, using timestamped visual history and exact streaming inference for long-horizon robot manipulation.

title: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy
summary: DeepRoboticsLab/sdk_deploy provides deployment code for taking robot policies from simulation into both sim-to-sim testing and real Deep Robotics hardware. It currently targets the M20 and Lite3 robots, making it useful as a bridge between trained control policies and practical validation on supported quadruped platforms.

extra.full_text: Sim-to-sim and sim-to-real deployment for Deep Robotics Robots, currently supporting M20 and Lite3

title: abmoRobotics/RLRoverLab
summary: RLRoverLab provides rover and space-focused reinforcement learning environments built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab. It looks useful for training and evaluating embodied control policies in simulated planetary-style robotics settings, especially where researchers want Isaac-compatible tasks rather than building rover environments from scratch.

extra.full_text: Rover and space-related reinforcement learning environments implemented for Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab.

title: jiteshsaini/robotics-level-4
summary: Raspberry Pi robot software for the Earth Rover Level 4 platform, updated for Raspberry Pi OS Trixie, runs on-board vision and ML for detection, tracking, human following, image classification, and Teachable Machine gesture recognition. It is aimed at building a self-contained rover that can perceive and react locally on the Pi, with optional Coral acceleration for faster inference.

title: castacks/AirStack
summary: AirStack is an agent-native robotics framework aimed at moving embodied AI from simulation to field hardware quickly, using a closed-loop workflow that mirrors the real robot one-to-one. It emphasizes self-validation and rapid sim-to-real iteration, making it useful for teams deploying field robotics systems where autonomy code needs to be tested against hardware-facing constraints rather than only offline simulation.

extra.full_text: Agent-native framework for rapid sim-to-real deployment of embodied AI for field robotics. Closed-loop, one-to-one workflow with hardware, self validating. Checkout develop branch for latest features.

title: kuds/mesozoic-labs
summary: Mesozoic Labs is an open-source platform for studying dinosaur biomechanics through MuJoCo-based Gymnasium environments, using reinforcement learning to train and evaluate locomotion behaviors. It includes curriculum learning and W&B experiment tracking, making it useful both for simulation experiments and for exploring eventual sim-to-real transfer into robotic systems inspired by extinct animals.

extra.full_text: Open-source research platform for dinosaur biomechanics and robotic locomotion using reinforcement learning. MuJoCo-based Gymnasium environments with curriculum learning, W&B experiment tracking, and sim-to-real transfer goals.

summary: mimic-lite targets efficient whole-body motion tracking for humanoid robots, with an emphasis on scaling up training and making the learned behavior usable in sim-to-real deployment. summary: rl-garden is a PyTorch-native, GPU-first framework for robot learning that brings reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and diffusion/flow policy methods into one toolkit.
